answer: Hamas's 1988 Covenant says the land of Palestine is a waqf that may not be given up, that peaceful solutions contradict its principles, and quotes a saying about fighting Jews. Its 2017 document is milder: it accepts a state on the 1967 lines as a 'formula of national consensus' and says its conflict is with Zionism, not with Jews. But it still says there shall be no recognition of Israel and rejects any alternative to liberating Palestine 'from the river to the sea'. After 7 October 2023 a Hamas leader said it would do it 'again and again'. Our reading: Hamas uses the phrase for a claim to all the land, with no recognition of Israel.

could_not_verify: The 2017 document's Arabic original and Hamas's own site; the English text is quoted from Middle East Eye's full publication, which is a news site.
Whether Hamas ever formally repealed the 1988 Covenant: no source read says it did, and Azzam Tamimi says the 2017 text would only 'practically' replace it.
The original LBC interview video of Ghazi Hamad (24 October 2023, in Arabic); quotes are from English news reports that rely on MEMRI's translation.
Statements by other Hamas leaders after 7 October; one 2025 Hamad interview is cited through RNZ (from CNN).
Scholars of the 2017 document: the RAND piece and a Times of Israel analysis could not be fetched. Each position in 'contested' rests on one think-tank paper and one quoted analyst in Al Jazeera.

Who translated the English texts: the Avalon page for the 1988 Covenant and Middle East Eye's 2017 text name no translator. In the Avalon text, '(killing the Jews)' in Article 7 is a parenthesis inside the English translation, not part of the quoted saying as such; a disputed rendering that the card does not rest on.

Ghazi Hamad's own words in Arabic. The Las Vegas Review-Journal item is a Newsmax story (declared as wire) and Ynetnews carries MEMRI's clip (declared as wire): MEMRI is an advocacy organisation, so three of the four sources for fact 5 rest on one interview and probably one translation; the Jerusalem Post is the only one that reports it in its own words, and it adds that Hamad 'largely deflected' when NBC asked him to clarify a week later.

Sources for facts 0 to 2 that carry the Covenant's specific articles: the Council on Foreign Relations, Middle East Institute and Wilson Center pages support only the general description of the 1988 charter, not the waqf, 'peaceful solutions' or Article 7 wording.
not_claimed: This card does not say that Palestinians as a people, or the PLO, hold Hamas's views; it describes Hamas's documents only.
It does not say that everyone who chants the phrase endorses Hamas.
It does not say Hamas has not changed at all: the 2017 document differs from the 1988 one, and the card lists how.
It does not quote Hamas's statements as a verdict on the war; Hamas's own leaders' words are cited as they were reported.

answer_claims.says: Hamas's 1988 Covenant says the land of Palestine is a waqf that may not be given up, that peaceful solutions contradict its principles, and quotes a saying about fighting Jews.
Its 2017 document is milder: it accepts a state on the 1967 lines as a 'formula of national consensus' and says its conflict is with Zionism, not with Jews.
But it still says there shall be no recognition of Israel and rejects any alternative to liberating Palestine 'from the river to the sea'.
After 7 October 2023 a Hamas leader said it would do it 'again and again'.
Our reading: Hamas uses the phrase for a claim to all the land, with no recognition of Israel.

skeptic.notes: Round 1. All quotes are on their pages and in context. Strongest objection from the chanting side: the 2017 document is quoted without its tone, but the card does carry the 1967-lines state, the 'not against Jews' paragraph and the Muslim Brotherhood change, and both scholarly readings sit in contested; fair. Strongest objection from the Jewish side: fact 5 (Hamad, 'again and again') rests on one LBCI interview and one translation (MEMRI, an advocacy group; Newsmax and Ynetnews copy it), the fourth source (RNZ/CNN 'golden moment', a 2025 interview) does not support the fact at all, and JPost adds that Hamad 'largely deflected' when NBC asked him about it (must-fix: replace the RNZ source with one that supports the quote, or reword the fact to the interview alone). Declared 'wire': Newsmax (Las Vegas Review-Journal reprint) and MEMRI (Ynetnews), so the gate counts them once each. Facts 0 to 2: the Covenant wording is verified on the Avalon page (the only source of the three that carries it); CFR, MEI and Wilson Center support the general description only (should-fix: find a second source for waqf, Article 13 and Article 7). Translation: the Avalon and Middle East Eye texts are unattributed translations; noted. 'accepts a state on the 1967 lines' is Al Jazeera's and CNN's verb; the text says Hamas 'considers' it 'a formula of national consensus' (nit). Verdict weakened because of fact 5, not because a quote is false.

citer.notes: Removed: 'Scholars disagree whether 2017 was real moderation' (the disagreement is in contested, which is not a fact; no fact on the card carries it) and 'So when Hamas uses the phrase, it does not mean coexistence' (an inference stronger than the document, which also says Hamas does not fight Jews because they are Jewish): replaced by an 'Our reading' sentence limited to what facts 3 and 4 say. Remaining four sentences tie to facts 0 to 5.
